title: Modular privacy add-ons pricing experiment: à-la-carte vs bundles
creator: Liam O'Connor
description: Objective: validate a modular pricing model for enterprise privacy/residency commitments to reduce negotiation friction and increase self-serve conversion. We will offer discrete "Modular Privacy Add-Ons" (Subprocessor Attestation, Data Residency Slot, Short Retention Mode, SCC Certification, Enhanced Audit Logs) that customers can purchase à-la-carte or as part of pre-bundled tiers. Hypothesis: offering clear, priced add-ons will shorten sales cycles for mid-market customers and increase average contract value (ACV) for enterprise deals that only need a subset of commitments.
experiment_overview: Design two parallel GTM treatments over 6 weeks: (A) Pre-bundled privacy tiers (Standard, Compliance, Enterprise) with fixed pricing and (B) À-la-carte modular add-ons where customers select only required commitments. Expose treatment via pricing page, self-serve signup UI, and sales quoting tool. Track conversion funnel from quote to signed contract and negotiation redlines frequency.
modular_addons: Data residency slot (single region) - monthly surcharge
Short retention mode (30/90/180 day buckets) - percent discount on storage fee
SCC baseline activation (EU/UK) - one-time contract admin fee
Enhanced audit logs (90 day retention & audit-ready exports) - monthly
sample_pricing_matrix: Short retention mode: -10% storage fee for 90-day bucket; -20% for 30-day bucket
metrics_and_goals: Primary metric: signed contracts per cohort (conversion rate)
Business metrics: ACV uplift for modular customers, win-rate vs baseline, average number of add-ons selected
Operational metric: number of legal redlines related to privacy/residency clauses
Acceptable outcome: >=10% faster quote-to-sign and >=8% ACV uplift for modular cohort
success_criteria: Self-serve signup conversion for modular offering >= baseline conversion
Sales-assisted deals selecting modular add-ons reduce legal redlines by 20%
Engineering able to auto-provision residency slots and toggle short-retention within 2 sprints after pilot
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Legal redlines increase because ad-hoc combinations create ambiguous commitments -> Mitigation: produce canonical modular contract exhibits and a templated Addendum generator for legal team
Risk: Billing complexity for per-region residency slots -> Mitigation: scope billing telemetry changes and pilot with small set of sales-assisted customers first
Risk: Regulatory nuance across EU/UK/EEA -> Mitigation: Legal validation and conservative region mapping; initial pilot excludes APAC
implementation_notes: Contracts: single Addendum template with checkbox-driven exhibit generator (DocuSign-ready)
Console: add UI to select residency slot(s) at signup and show monthly delta in cost estimate
Billing: meter residency slots and audit logs separately; add line items in invoices
Runtime: engineering feature flags for residency toggle, retention policy enforcement, and per-customer KV cache isolation for residency compliance
timeline: Week 0: finalize modular contract exhibits and pricing bands
Week 1-2: implement console selection UI + pricing estimate and sales quoting template
Week 3: soft launch to invited self-serve customers and 5 sales-assisted pilot deals
Week 4-6: measure metrics, collect legal redlines, iterate pricing and contract language
acceptance_criteria: Contract exhibits approved by Legal and Security
Console shows residency & audit add-ons with accurate monthly delta
Billing creates distinct invoice line items for selected add-ons
Pilot includes at least 10 quotes and 3 signed deals for statistically actionable feedback

notes_for_reviewers: When reviewing pricing bands, prioritize simplicity and predictable renewal impact. Avoid per-token surcharges tied to residency (adds meter complexity). We prefer discrete line items or flat monthly surcharges for pilot to keep invoices readable for procurement teams.
